# Part 1: Explore album sales

```{r}
#Load Libraries

library("here")
library("tidyverse")

#Load data

rds_files <- c("b_lyrics.RDS", "ts_lyrics.RDS", "sales.RDS")

## Check whether we have all 3 files

if (any(!file.exists(here("data", rds_files)))) {
    ## If we don't, then download the data
    b_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/beyonce_lyrics.csv")
    ts_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/taylor_swift_lyrics.csv")
    sales <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/sales.csv")

    ## Then save the data objects to RDS files
    saveRDS(b_lyrics, file = here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(ts_lyrics, file = here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(sales, file = here("data", "sales.RDS"))
}

#Load data

b_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
ts_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
sales <- readRDS(here("data", "sales.RDS"))

```

## Part 1A

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)

#Step 1: create new released column in "sales"

#check current class of released
class(sales$released)

#create regex to remove parentheses and brackets
sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(released = str_remove(released, 
  "\\s*\\(.*\\)+\\s*\\[.*\\]"))

  # \\s*: find any whitespace before the parentheses or brackets
#\\(, \\[: find either an opening 
#parenthesis ( or an opening bracket [
#.*: find any characters within () or []
# +: does it for both parenthesis AND brackets
#\\), \\]: find either a closing parenthesis 
# ) or a closing bracket ]

#change class of released_new to date
sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(released = mdy(released))

#confirm           
class(sales$released)

#list distinct countries 
distinct_country <- sales %>% 
  select(country) %>% 
  distinct()

# Step 2: Create a factor called 'country'
sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(country = fct_collapse(country,
              `US` = c("US"),
              `UK` = c("UK"),
              `World` = c("World", "WW"),
              `Other` = c("AUS", "JPN",
                          "CAN","FRA","FR")))
#collapse all other countries into other

# Step 3: transform sales into unit (millions)

sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(sales= sales / 1e6)

# Step 4: Keep only UK,US, and World
sales <- sales %>%
  filter(country %in% c("US", "UK", "World"))

# Print the final wrangled tibble
as_tibble(sales)

```

## Part 1B

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# Assuming 'sales' is your previously wrangled data frame

# Step 1: Keep only album sales from the US
us_sales <- sales %>%
  filter(country == "US")

# Step 2: Create a new column called years_since_release
us_sales <- us_sales %>%
  mutate(years_since_release = floor(interval(released, today()) / years(1)))  # Calculate years since release
#floor used to round to nearest whole number

# Step 3: calculate most recent, oldest, and median years since release
us_sales_stats <- us_sales %>%
  summarize(
    most_recent = min(years_since_release, na.rm = TRUE),
    oldest = max(years_since_release, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_years = median(years_since_release, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the summary statistics
print(us_sales_stats)

```

## Part 1C

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Assuming 'sales' is your wrangled data frame from Part 1A

# Step 1: Calculate total album sales for each artist and each country
total_sales <- sales %>%
  group_by(artist, country) %>%
  summarize(total_sales_millions = sum(sales, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') 

# .groups : overrides default and drops 
# grouping by first argument (artist)

# Step 2: Calculate the percentage of total sales by artist
total_sales <- total_sales %>%
  group_by(artist) %>%
  mutate(percentage_sales = total_sales_millions / sum(total_sales_millions) * 100)

# Step 3: Create a percent stacked bar chart
ggplot(total_sales, aes(x = artist, y = percentage_sales, fill = country)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Percentage of Album Sales by Artist and Country",
       subtitle = "More than 50% of sales for both artists are international, excluding the UK",
       x = "Artist",
       y = "Percentage of Sales (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 100)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank(),
         plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face= "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text (face="bold"))

```

## Part 1D

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)


# Step 1: Filter for World sales and keep only necessary columns 
world_sales <- sales %>%
  filter(country == "World") %>%
  select(title, artist, sales)

# Step 2: Order the album titles by sales (from most to least)
world_sales <- world_sales %>%
  mutate(title = fct_reorder(title, sales, .desc = TRUE))

# Step 3: Create the bar plot
ggplot(world_sales, aes(x = title, y = sales, fill = artist)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +  # Flips the axes to make album titles readable
  labs(title = "Global Album Sales by Artist",
       subtitle= "Dangerously in Love and Fearless were highest selling albums for Beyonce and Taylor, respectively",
       x = "Album Title",
       y = "Sales (in millions)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme( legend.title= element_text(size=16, face= "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face= "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text (face="bold")    )  # Adjust text size for readability

```

## Part 1E

```{r}

# Step 1: Filter to keep necessary columns 
sales_by_release <- sales %>%
  select(title, artist, released, sales, country)

# Step 2: Create the scatter plot
ggplot(sales_by_release, aes(x = released, y = sales, color = artist)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +  # Adjust size of points
  labs(title = "Sales of Studio Albums by Release Date",
       subtitle= "Highest album sales for US,UK, and the rest of world was in 2008",
       x = "Release Date",
       y = "Sales (in millions)") +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free_y") +  # Facet by country with free y-axis scales
  theme_gray() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
        legend.title= element_text(size=16, face= "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face= "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text (face="bold"))

```

# Part 2: Exploring Sentiment of Lyrics

# Part 2A

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidytext)

# Use "lines" token to tokenize lyrics column

tidy_ts_lyrics <- ts_lyrics %>%
  unnest_tokens(
    output=line, #creates new column called 'line'
    input= Lyrics, #replaces 'Lyrics' with output 'line'
    token = "lines")  

#How many lines contain "hello"?

library(stringr)

# Step 1: Count lines containing "hello"
hello_lines <- tidy_ts_lyrics %>%
  filter(str_detect(line, "hello")) 

print(hello_lines)

#step 2: Count the total number of lines containing "hello"
count_hello <- nrow(hello_lines) 
cat("Total rows containing 'hello':", count_hello) 
#prints "total rows..." 
#with sum of rows 

#How many lines contain "goodbye"?

# Step 1: Count lines containing "goodbye"
goodbye_lines <- tidy_ts_lyrics %>%
  filter(str_detect(line, "goodbye"))

print(goodbye_lines)

# step 2: Count the total number of lines containing "goodbye"
count_goodbye <- nrow(goodbye_lines)
cat("Total rows containing 'goodbye':", count_goodbye)

```
